resources.string: Choose the connection system shown on the car screen. Changing it restarts the connection if FT is on.
Open ICCOA Carlink on the car, then choose your car below.
Wireless connection via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. Search for your car and enter its code on the Home tab.
Open ICCOA Carlink on the car, then connect to its device below. Keep Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and Location on. Android may ask you to join the car Wi-Fi.
Looking for the car — up to 60 seconds
Search complete — choose your car below
Checking device services — up to 15 seconds
Turn on Bluetooth, then tap Scan again
Allow Nearby devices and precise Location for FT, then tap Scan again.
Turn on Location, then tap Scan again
Connection check failed — send a report to the developer
Choose your car while ICCOA Carlink is open on its screen. Other nearby Bluetooth devices may also appear.
Enter the six-digit code shown on the car screen. Use the current code, including any leading zeroes.
The connection is ready. Wait for FT on the car screen. If Android asks to share your screen for sound or phone mirroring, choose the entire screen and confirm.
The Bluetooth call profile (HFP) is not connected.
Call connection has not been verified
ICCOA projection is connected, but calls through the car are unavailable. In Bluetooth settings, select your car and enable Phone calls (HFP).
To hear calls through the car, select it in Bluetooth settings and enable Phone calls (HFP).
Allow Nearby devices for FT to check the call connection.
Could not check the call connection. Check it in Bluetooth settings.
Call audio uses Bluetooth separately from ICCOA. In Bluetooth settings, select your car and enable Phone calls. Make sure the connected device shown here is your car.
